description:
**`chief list` in this repo prints two live tasklists followed by ninety-four `done` ones, and nothing on screen distinguishes a park from a block from a ready.** The signal is 2% of the output and it is at the top only by luck of the sort. In `cuneiform` — 371 tasklists, 312 done — the live work is under 16% of the lines. An operator's actual question is *what can I run right now*, and the command named `list` answers it worst of the three commands that could.

`97-tasklist-state-report` deliberately left this alone, and its reason is binding on how this is done rather than on whether: *"`chief list` keeps working exactly as it does now. It is a different tool — per-tasklist story progress, not aggregate state — and scripts and habits depend on its output."* Both halves of that hold. `chief status` is the aggregate; `chief list` is per-tasklist and should stay per-tasklist. **So the change is presentation and default scope, not a merge of the two commands, and the script contract must survive it** — `scripts/tasklist-census.py --plain` in `~/Development` is the precedent for how: pretty for a human, stable and parseable on demand.

Second half, same complaint one level over: `chief ps` shows RUNNING drivers, which is correct and is why it is called `ps`. But there is no view of everything in flight — running plus ready plus blocked plus parked, minus the done — for a single repo. That is the thing an operator looks at before deciding what to start, and today it takes `chief list`, `chief status --blocked` and reading park prose to assemble.

Nothing here is new state. Every fact needed is already computed by `status.sh` for its own table, including the dependency verdicts behind BLOCKED and the park reasons behind PARKED. **This is a rendering and default-scope story; if it grows a new source of truth, it has gone wrong.**
warmup: chief list | head -20; echo '---'; chief list | wc -l

userStories.title: `chief list` defaults to the work that is still live
acceptanceCriteria: By default `chief list` omits completed tasklists. `-a`/`--all` restores them. In this repo that is 96 lines down to 2; in cuneiform, 371 down to 59.

The default must not hide anything an operator could act on. Ready, in-progress, blocked and PARKED all remain — parked especially, since a park is a decision waiting on a human and hiding it is how twenty of them accumulated unnoticed.
A count of what was omitted is printed, so the shorter output never reads as a smaller portfolio. Silent truncation is the failure mode.
The done-by-default change is documented in the CHANGELOG as a behaviour change to a long-stable command, not slipped in as a formatting tweak.
userStories.notes: Implemented live-by-default listing: completed tasklists are omitted with an explicit count, --all restores them, parked rows remain, and CHANGELOG.md documents the behavior change. Verified with bash -n, test/status-deps.sh, test/park-reasons.sh, test/doc-sync.sh, test/version-bump.sh, and git diff --check; all green (shellcheck unavailable).

userStories.title: It is formatted as a table, and machines get a stable contract
acceptanceCriteria: Human output is a column-aligned table in the house style already set by `scripts/tasklist-census.py` and `chief status` — at minimum name, state, story progress, category, and for a park or a block the reason in the operator's terms. Reuse the existing rendering; a third table style in this codebase is a defect, not a feature.
STATE is visually distinguishable at a glance, not inferable from a progress fraction: today `0/3` is printed identically for a tasklist that is ready to run and one that is blocked on a dependency.

`--plain` emits stable, parseable, unaligned output for scripts, on the same rationale as the census script's flag. `97` declined to touch this command because 'scripts and habits depend on its output', and this flag is what makes that safe.
A test asserts `--plain` is stable across the formatting change — the counterfactual is a downstream script silently breaking on box-drawing characters.
Non-TTY output must not emit colour or box-drawing by default. A piped `chief list` that ships escape codes is the same bug in a different costume.
userStories.notes: Implemented aligned human columns (name/state/progress/category/reason) and stable tab-delimited --plain output; status.sh JSON supplies blocked dependency reasons and parked rows retain reasons. status-deps fixture test: green; bash -n, doc-sync, version-bump, quality ratchet, doc-link ratchet, and git diff --check: green; shellcheck unavailable.

userStories.title: `chief ps -a` shows everything in flight, not only what has a driver
acceptanceCriteria: `chief ps -a` shows all non-done tasklists — running, ready, blocked, parked — while bare `chief ps` keeps its current meaning of live drivers across all repos. A command called `ps` that stopped showing processes would be worse than the gap it closed.

The live-run detail `ps` already renders — zone-hold reasons, approval commands, diff-budget warnings, stall detection, the UNREGISTERED-driver flag — is preserved unchanged for the rows that have a driver. This story adds rows; it must not thin the ones that matter most.
A blocked row names what blocks it and a parked row names its reason, both from the verdicts `status.sh` already computes. No new dependency resolution is written for this view.
`chief monitor` renders the same view under `-a`, since a live-refreshing view of only the running subset has the same blind spot.
A test drives a fixture repo containing one of each state and asserts every one appears under `-a` and that the done ones do not.
